paper_metadata.title: Enhanced fatigue performance of γ/γ′ dual-phase single-crystal superalloys with graded surface nanostructures

The SX alloy ingots (15 mm in diameter and 150 mm in length) were fabricated in a directional solidification furnace.

other.steps: 1290 °C for 1 h, then 1300 °C for 2 h, 1315 °C for 4 h

evidence.quote: the ingots were subjected to standard heat treatments as follows [ 31 ]: 1290 ◦ C for 1 h, then 1300 ◦ C for 2 h, 1315 ◦ C for 4 h, air-cooling
1120 ◦ C for 4 h, air-cooling + 870 ◦ C for 32 h, and finally air-cooling to eliminate dendritic segregation and achieve a unimodal size distribution of cuboidal γ ′ precipitates.
1120 ◦ C for 4 h, air-cooling + 870 ◦ C for 32 h, and finally air-cooling to eliminate dendritic segregation and achieve a unimodal size distribution of cuboidal γ ′ precipitates.

other.specimen: notched rotating-bending fatigue bars, stress concentration factor 1.7

evidence.quote: notched rotating-bending fatigue bars with a theoretical stress concentration factor of 1.7 were processed by electrical discharge machining and mechanical machining.

The shots used in the present study were zirconia ceramic beads with an average diameter of 0.3 mm. The pressure of the shots was estimated to be approximately 0.2 MPa, the velocity of the shot flow was ~30 m/s, and the processing duration was 60 s.

evidence.section: 3.1. Initial microstructure of non-treated SX base material
evidence.quote: γ channels with a mean channel width of ~80 nm

evidence.section: 3.1. Initial microstructure of non-treated SX base material
evidence.quote: well-shaped cuboidal γ ′ precipitates with an average size of ~580 nm

evidence.section: 3.1. Initial microstructure of non-treated SX base material
evidence.quote: a typical dual-phase architecture is composed of well-shaped cuboidal γ ′ precipitates with an average size of ~580 nm and γ channels with a mean channel width of ~80 nm

attributes.size: ~0.3-1 μm thickness; average grain size ~55 nm

evidence.quote: (i) fully nanocrystallized zone (FNZ) at the topmost surface (~0.3 – 1 μ m thickness)
(ii) transition zone (TZ, ~0.6 μ m thickness)

attributes.size: reaching at least 8 μm in depth

evidence.quote: (iii) partially nanocrystallized γ channels zone (PN γ CZ, reaching at least 8 μ m in depth) with increased local misorientations and high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, > 10 ◦ ) along γ / γ ′ interfaces
Well-defined intersecting slip bands that have been extensively reported in SP-treated alloys [ 26 , 38 ] are visible within 0 – 100 μ m beneath the surface.

evidence.section: 3.2. Mechanical properties of non-treated and SP-treated SX samples
evidence.quote: reveals the formation of a work-hardened region extending up to a depth of ~250 μ m

attributes.location: near slip bands and surface region

evidence.quote: geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density ( ρ GND ), estimated from the kernel average misorientation (KAM) values, are significantly higher near the slip bands

evidence.section: 3.2. Mechanical properties of non-treated and SP-treated SX samples
evidence.quote: the SP-treated samples have an average fatigue life of 5.8 × 10 5 cycles, about 6 times as long as that of the non-treated base material (1.0 × 10 5 cycles)

evidence.section: 3.2. Mechanical properties of non-treated and SP-treated SX samples
evidence.quote: This indicates that SP treatment can improve the surface hardness by 53.7 %.

The graded surface nanostructures, together with work hardening and compressive residual stress, hindered strain localization and delayed crack initiation in the original soft γ matrix channels, thus prolonging the fatigue life.
